zh: 历史中的战争、灾害和人物选择，并不总能从长期结构直接推导出来。某次事件可能改变原有方向，让社会进入此前没有走过的道路。承认结构的重要，不等于取消偶然的作用。
但是，偶然也不是在空白中发生。同样的冲击进入不同的制度、资源和关系网络，可能产生不同后果。一个决定能否留下长期影响，取决于它后来怎样被组织、复制和维持。
早期形成的道路、规则或知识安排，会影响后来的选择。人们已经投入资源，也学会围绕原有方式合作，转向新道路便需要付出成本。路径依赖解释这种累积，却不意味着过去已经封闭未来。
理解文明分化，需要同时看见事件与积累。偶发变化可以开启新的方向，既有能力也会限制或支持这种转向。历史既不是一套必然展开的程序，也不是彼此毫无联系的意外。
en: Wars, disasters and personal choices cannot always be deduced from long-term structures. An event may redirect a society toward a path it has not previously taken. Recognizing structural conditions does not eliminate contingency.

Yet contingency does not act on an empty field. The same shock can have different consequences within different institutions, resources and networks. Whether a decision leaves a lasting mark depends on how it is subsequently organized, reproduced and maintained.

Established routes, rules and knowledge shape later choices. Resources have already been invested, and people have learned to cooperate in familiar ways. Changing direction therefore carries costs. Path dependence explains this accumulation without implying that the past has closed the future.

Understanding divergence requires attention to both events and accumulated conditions. An unexpected change can open a direction that existing capabilities support or constrain. History is neither an inevitable program nor a sequence of unrelated accidents.

zh: 定居意味着越来越多的未来被留在同一个地点。房屋、储存、土地和设施需要维护，人们也必须处理使用权、继承和分配。生活不再只取决于眼前能够带走什么，而开始依赖长期投入。
农业把食物生产与季节、土地和劳动联系起来。储存使剩余可以跨越时间，却也产生谁能够进入仓储、怎样征集和怎样分配的问题。权力由此与管理资源的能力更紧密地结合。
城市把这些关系推向新的密度。专业劳动、交换、宗教与行政相互靠近，而城市又依赖周围地区持续供给。它并非一个人口更多的村落，而是一种需要协调陌生人与不同活动的社会空间。
这些变化没有为所有地区规定同一条道路。定居、农业、剩余和城市可以以不同节奏组合。理解早期文明，重要的是看清这些能力怎样连接，而不是把每个社会放进相同的阶段表。
en: Settlement binds more of the future to one place. Houses, storage, land and infrastructure require maintenance, while communities must organize use, inheritance and distribution. Life increasingly depends on lasting investment rather than only on what people can carry away.

Agriculture links food production to seasons, land and labor. Storage carries surplus through time, but also raises questions about access, collection and distribution. Power becomes more closely associated with the capacity to manage resources.

Cities intensify these relationships. Specialized work, exchange, religion and administration become concentrated while depending on continuing supplies from surrounding areas. A city is more than a populous village: it must coordinate strangers and different kinds of activity.

These changes do not prescribe one route for every region. Settlement, agriculture, surplus and cities can combine at different tempos. The task is to understand how these capabilities connect, rather than place every society on an identical sequence of stages.

zh: 苏美尔的重要性，不在于用一个“最早”概括所有复杂社会，而在于城市把许多能力集中到了一起。神庙、仓储、手工业、贸易和行政彼此依赖，多个城市国家则在竞争、合作和战争中共同构成一个世界。
南部两河的城市与农业腹地保持资源往来，也需要从外部取得木材、石材和金属。水利维护要求内部组织，原料需求又推动远距离交换。城市从一开始便同时面对内部协调和外部依赖。
粮食、劳动力和物品流动越复杂，记录的价值越高。文字与账目让征集、分配和责任更容易被保存和追踪。它们并非单纯的文化装饰，而与城市管理的具体问题紧密相连。
这也说明文字不能脱离制度来解释。记录需要书写者、用途和持续维护的组织。苏美尔呈现的，是多种能力相互支持的高密度结构，而不是一项发明独自创造整个文明。
en: Sumer matters not because one claim of being first can explain every complex society, but because cities concentrated many capabilities. Temples, storage, crafts, trade and administration depended on one another. Competing and cooperating city-states together formed a connected world.

Southern Mesopotamian cities exchanged resources with agricultural hinterlands and obtained timber, stone and metals from elsewhere. Irrigation maintenance demanded internal organization, while raw materials encouraged distant exchange. Cities faced coordination at home and dependence abroad from the outset.

As movements of food, labor and goods became more complex, records became more valuable. Writing and accounts made collection, distribution and responsibility easier to preserve and trace. They were closely connected to practical problems of urban administration.

Writing therefore needs to be understood alongside institutions. Records require trained writers, purposes and organizations that maintain their use. Sumer illustrates a dense combination of mutually supporting capabilities, rather than one invention independently creating a civilization.

zh: 河流能够支持农业与交通，却没有让早期文明形成同一种政治结构。尼罗河沿线的人口、运输和农业具有较强的纵向联系，给埃及的整合提供了特殊条件。这些条件仍需要通过王权、宗教与组织才能发挥作用。
埃及的长期连续并不意味着制度从未变化。王朝更替、分裂和重建之中，农业、神庙、书写与神圣王权不断进入新的政治安排。可以持续的，是若干相互支持的能力和记忆，而非一个完全不变的国家。
印度河的城市建设显示高度组织能力，但留下的材料并不足以让我们确定所有政治和知识结构。城市化程度不能替代缺失的证据。未知应当保留，而不是用别处的王权或宗教模式填补。
中国早期文明同样需要放在多个区域的联系中理解。黄河、长江及其他重要区域的城市、礼制与整合过程，不能被压成一条河流的单独故事。比较河流文明，应比较具体组织条件，而非从水系直接推导制度。
en: Rivers supported agriculture and transport without producing one political form. The Nile linked population, movement and farming along a pronounced axis, creating distinctive conditions for Egyptian integration. Kingship, religion and organization were still necessary to make use of those conditions.

Egyptian continuity did not mean unchanging institutions. Across dynastic change, fragmentation and reconstruction, agriculture, temples, writing and sacred kingship entered new political arrangements. What persisted was a combination of capabilities and memories, not an entirely unchanged state.

Indus cities demonstrate substantial organizational capacity, but surviving material does not establish every feature of political or intellectual life. Urban sophistication cannot replace missing evidence. Unknowns should remain open rather than be filled with models of kingship or religion borrowed from elsewhere.

Early Chinese civilization also requires attention to connections among regions. Cities, ritual and integration in the Yellow River, Yangtze and other areas cannot be reduced to the story of one river. Comparison should examine particular organizational conditions instead of deriving institutions directly from waterways.

zh: 美洲早期复杂社会提醒我们，文明并不需要复制欧亚大陆的条件才能出现。不同的动物、作物、地形和交通条件下，人们仍能组织大型聚落、公共建筑、交换和政治生活。缺少某种熟悉技术，不等于缺少复杂性。
安第斯地区的海岸、高地与山谷提供不同资源。连接这些生态带，可以形成不同于大片平原农业的组织方式。中美洲也有自身的积累和节奏，因此“美洲文明”不能被当作一个统一时间表。
非洲的复杂社会同样不应只沿尼罗河和地中海寻找。不同区域的农业、牧业、交换和政治组织，需要在当地条件与外部联系中观察。把一个地区当作所有地区的标准，会让其他道路变得不可见。
早期城市文明共有协调人口、资源和记忆的问题，却可以采取不同答案。共同能力并不必然产生共同制度。文明史的第一次分叉，正是在这些不同条件和选择不断积累时展开的。
en: Early complex societies in the Americas show that civilization did not require a reproduction of Eurasian conditions. Different animals, crops, terrain and transport arrangements still supported large settlements, public buildings, exchange and political life. The absence of a familiar technology is not the absence of complexity.

Andean coasts, highlands and valleys offered different resources. Connecting ecological zones supported arrangements unlike those based on broad agricultural plains. Mesoamerica had its own accumulations and rhythms, so the Americas cannot be assigned a single civilizational timetable.

African complexity likewise cannot be sought only along the Nile and Mediterranean. Regional farming, pastoralism, exchange and political organization must be understood through local conditions and external connections. Making one region the standard hides other paths.

Early urban societies shared problems of coordinating people, resources and memory, but could answer them differently. Common capabilities did not entail identical institutions. Civilizational divergence unfolded as those different conditions and choices accumulated.

zh: 青铜时代的政治地图可以分成许多王国，资源网络却早已越过疆界。铜、锡、木材与粮食并不集中在一个地方，城市和宫殿需要矿区、运输者、商人和港口持续合作。远方的条件开始影响本地能够做什么。
交换还需要政治保障。外交、礼物与彼此承认，使不同强权有可能维持联系。一个政治上并不庞大的节点，也可能因为处在关键通道而具有远超疆域的影响。
这种连接能够增加能力，也会传递困难。供应和交通受到冲击时，依赖它们的组织会承受压力；原本局部的问题可能通过联系扩散。青铜时代崩解应放在这种脆弱性中理解，而不能归结为一个能够解释所有地方的单一原因。
崩解也不等于所有文明同时消失。不同区域、城市和制度的损失、适应与继承并不一致。必须区分政治中心的终止、网络的重组和仍在继续的社会生活，才能看清危机如何改变了世界。
en: Bronze Age political maps contained separate kingdoms, but resource networks already crossed their borders. Copper, tin, timber and grain were not concentrated in one place. Cities and palaces depended on continuing cooperation among mines, carriers, merchants and ports. Distant conditions affected local capabilities.

Exchange also needed political support. Diplomacy, gifts and mutual recognition could sustain relations among powers. A modest political center could exert influence far beyond its territory by occupying an important route.

These connections increased capabilities while transmitting difficulties. Disrupted supplies and transport placed pressure on dependent organizations, allowing local problems to spread. Bronze Age breakdown needs to be understood within this vulnerability, rather than reduced to one cause explaining every region.

Breakdown did not mean that every civilization disappeared simultaneously. Loss, adaptation and inheritance differed among regions, cities and institutions. Political termination, network reorganization and continuing social life must be distinguished to understand how the crisis changed the world.

zh: 铁器的意义，不在于某一天突然取代青铜，而在于生产、加工和复制逐渐变得更加稳定。较广泛的原料分布提供了新的可能，但木炭、工匠与技术仍然不可缺少。材料改变条件，不会自动生成新的政治制度。
亚述显示了高强度军事组织能够怎样扩大政治尺度。扩张要求持续动员资源，也使治理、运输与控制面对更大的压力。征服的范围与长期协调的能力，不能被视作同一个指标。
波斯则让我们观察大型帝国怎样处理内部差异。维持广阔空间中的秩序，并不一定意味着让所有地方完全相同。不同区域与群体之间需要形成能够持续运作的联系。
周代世界中的诸侯、礼制和分层权威，提供了另一种组织方式。把这些社会放在一起，并不是为早期帝国排出优劣，而是看见材料、军事与制度可以怎样组合，以及每种组合需要承担什么成本。
en: Iron mattered not because it suddenly replaced bronze on one day, but because its production, working and reproduction gradually became more reliable. More widely available ores opened possibilities, while charcoal, skilled workers and technique remained essential. Materials changed conditions without automatically creating institutions.

Assyria illustrates how intensive military organization could expand political scale. Expansion required continuing resource mobilization and increased pressures on government, transport and control. The reach of conquest and the capacity for lasting coordination are not the same measure.

Persia offers a view of how a large empire could manage internal differences. Sustaining order across extensive territories did not necessarily require making every locality identical. Regions and groups needed connections that could continue to function.

The Zhou world of regional rulers, ritual and layered authority offered another arrangement. Comparing these societies is not a ranking of early empires. It reveals different combinations of materials, military organization and institutions, along with the costs each combination carried.
